title: Total open Čech resolution comparison with derived evaluation
statement: Let X be any scheme, i:X.Opens → X.Etale a cover-preserving finite-limit-preserving functor, with i(top) terminal. Let U be a finite u-small open family with supremum top. Let G be any étale abelian sheaf in universe u+1, assume its sheaf category has injective resolutions, and let I be any injective resolution of G. For each n≥0 the degree-n homology of the total of the actual double complex D=C^p(U,i^*I^q) [def-sc-etale-open-cech-resolution-double-complex] is isomorphic to (R^n ev_i(top))(G). Neither separatedness, affine opens, nor acyclicity of G is assumed; the assertion involves the total resolution and not the sections Čech complex.

source.place: Original proof step 2: the injective Čech augmentation and total-complex abutment comparison

proof.text: The open cover generates a covering sieve on top. Push it forward using cover preservation to obtain a cover of i(top). Finite-limit preservation identifies products over i(top) with i applied to intersections; universal uniqueness makes these identifications commute with every projection and hence every Čech face. If needed to apply the existing large-index interface, lift the cover index by ULift and transport products along its canonical equivalence.

Augment the horizontal row C^bullet(U,i^*I^q) by I^q(i(top)) via restrictions. The sheaf condition computes H^0 and injective Čech acyclicity computes the positive groups as zero. The product comparisons from the preceding step identify these rows with the image-cover Čech complexes. Thus each row augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism, including empty covers.

Naturality of restriction makes the row augmentations a morphism from the evaluated resolution to D.X 0 and then to Tot D by inclusion of the (0,q) summand. Its horizontal differential is zero and its vertical sign is +1. Apply the first-quadrant column-augmentation theorem to conclude that the total augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. This theorem uses the finite diagonal filtration, so it does not assume a bound on the length of I.

Invert the homology isomorphism of that augmentation and compose with the inverse of I.isoRightDerivedObj for the sheaf-evaluation functor in degree n. This identifies total homology with the displayed derived evaluation.
